title: Registration Officer
description: Registration Officer Black Hills State University Black Hills State University invites internal applications for a Registration Officer to support accurate student academic records, effective registrar operations, and responsive service to students and the campus community. This position combines technical expertise, analytical judgment, and collaboration to help students navigate registration requirements and progress toward graduation. The Registration Officer manages registration updates; evaluates and articulates transfer coursework; evaluates and awards credit for prior learning; maintains grades and transcripts; and supports graduation processing. reviewing and correcting records for external enrollment reporting, and calculating student-athlete academic eligibility. Working closely with students, faculty, academic departments, advising and student-success staff, Athletics, and system partners, the Registration Officer interprets and applies institutional and South Dakota Board of Regents requirements. The position resolves academic record and registration issues, safeguards confidential information, maintains accurate public and internal resources, supports and trains office staff, and makes assigned operational decisions in the Registrar’s absence. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  Knowledge of: the administrative responsibilities, principles, and practices of the registrar’s office; Effective methods of administering and updating records systems; Courses and grades required for graduation in specific disciplines; Ability to develop and organize accurate record maintenance processes; Maintain correct student educational records. Communicate information clearly and concisely; Regular and reliable attendance. Initiative, self-management, and decision-making skills Able to evaluate multiple competing tasks Excellent customer service skills SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES WILL DEMONSTRATE: Knowledge of registrar operations, academic records administration, higher education curriculum procedures, and graduation requirements. Ability to maintain accurate student records and develop effective processes for managing and updating records systems. Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and sound judgment when applying policies and resolving complex issues. Clear, concise communication and excellent customer service. Initiative, effective self-management, and the ability to prioritize multiple competing responsibilities.  A commitment to confidentiality, collaborative service, and regular, reliable attendance. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience using the Ellucian Banner student information system Experience interpreting South Dakota Board of Regents Policy and FERPA Experience evaluating and applying athletic eligibility requirements SPECIAL COMMENTS: Sponsorship not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications must be made at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Please attach a cover letter, resume and the names and contact information of at least three professional references. title: University Registrar
description: University Registrar Black Hills State University | Spearfish, South Dakota Black Hills State University invites applications for University Registrar. The Registrar leads the office responsible for student academic records, registration, transfer credit evaluation, academic catalogs, degree awarding, enrollment verification, and transcript services. This position protects the accuracy and confidentiality of student records while helping students, faculty, and staff navigate academic policies and processes. The University Registrar supervises office personnel; oversees registration, degree audits, and graduation processes; and works with Academic Affairs and campus partners to implement approved curriculum and improve student information systems. The Registrar also advises university leaders on academic records practices and ensures office operations comply with university, South Dakota Board of Regents, state, and federal requirements, including FERPA. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: a. Establish office priorities, procedures, service standards, and measures of effectiveness. b. Supervise, train, and evaluate staff; assign work and maintain coverage for critical academic deadlines. c. Develop the office budget, manage resources, document procedures, and plan for continuity of operations. d. Serve on University and Regental committees and advise campus leaders on registrar functions and the operational effects of proposed academic policies. e. Direct the creation, accuracy, security, correction, retention, and authorized release of student academic records. f. Oversee grades, academic standing actions, transcripts, enrollment and degree verifications, and other official record services. g. Interpret and implement applicable requirements under FERPA, SDBOR policies, university policies, and records retention schedules; coordinate complex questions with appropriate campus and system offices. h. Maintain controls and audit practices that protect record integrity and support accurate institutional reporting. i. Oversee registration processes, academic term setup, course section data, enrollment changes, withdrawals, and related student communications. j. Help develop and administer the academic calendar and ensure that published dates, deadlines, and procedures are accurate and consistent. k. Resolve escalated registration issues within approved policy and delegated authority. l. Coordinate implementation of approved programs, courses, prerequisites, and degree requirements in the catalog and student information system. m. Oversee production and maintenance of the academic catalog in partnership with Academic Affairs. o. Direct the recording and evaluation of transfer credit according to approved policies and articulation agreements. p. Maintain reliable degree audit rules and communicate the effects of curriculum changes to affected offices. q. Direct graduation application, degree audit, eligibility review, degree posting, diploma, and related record processes. r. Provide leadership to produce bi-annual Commencement exercises. t. Identify barriers or recurring errors in degree completion processes and recommend improvements. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: · Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. · Progressively responsible experience in a college or university registrar’s office or closely related academic administration, including experience supervising personnel or leading complex operations. · Demonstrated knowledge of academic records, registration, curriculum and degree requirements, and student information systems. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: · Master’s degree. · Experience leading multiple registrar functions at a university. · Experience with Ellucian Banner or a comparable student information system and with degree audit and catalog systems. · Experience implementing policy or system changes across multiple departments. · Knowledge of South Dakota Board of Regents policies and processes. SPECIAL COMMENTS: Sponsorship is not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications must be made at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Please attach a cover letter, resume and the names and contact information of at least three professional references. First review for this position will begin on November 15, 2026 at 11pm mountain time. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may be directed to John Allred at john.allred@bhsu.edu. Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu. title: Director, Student Support Services
description: Black Hills State University invites applications for the position of Director of Student Support Services. This leadership position is responsible for the overall administration of the federally funded TRIO Student Support Services program in accordance with federal regulations, the approved grant proposal, and University policies and procedures. The Director provides strategic and operational leadership for the program, ensuring that its goals and objectives are effectively developed, implemented, evaluated, and documented. The position selects, trains, and supervises program staff and student employees; develops and manages the annual federal grant budget; maintains accurate participant records; and prepares grant proposals, continuation applications, Annual Performance Reports, budget reports, and other required institutional and federal reports. Join Black Hills State University and help create meaningful opportunities for students to overcome barriers, achieve their educational goals, and thrive throughout their university experience. THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE: • Will be a student-centered and collaborative leader who demonstrates strong grant-management, budgeting, supervision, communication, and organizational abilities. • This individual will be committed to supporting student persistence and achievement while maintaining full compliance with federal grant requirements and University expectations. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE: • Coordinating, supervising, and evaluating program services and activities. • Determining student eligibility for participation in Student Support Services. • Advising a small caseload of students on course registration, FAFSA completion, study skills, academic planning, and related needs. • Providing or coordinating academic, financial, career, social, and personal support based on participant needs. • Advocating for students and ensuring equitable access and appropriate accommodations for students with disabilities and members of underrepresented populations. • Maintaining effective systems for documenting services, evaluating program performance, and measuring progress toward grant objectives. • Conducting follow-up with participants after they exit the program. • Developing strong working relationships with university administrators, faculty, and staff; vocational rehabilitation and disability services counselors; community resource providers; other postsecondary institutions; professional organizations; and government officials. • Serving as the primary liaison between program participants and campus or community partners. • Collaborating with University personnel to connect students with appropriate academic and skill-development resources. • Promoting Student Support Services to eligible students and increasing the program’s visibility both within and beyond the University. • Representing the program at University and community events, including events that support diversity and multicultural education. • Participating in administrative staff meetings and University planning initiatives. • Preparing institutional reports as directed by the Vice President for Enrollment Management. • Performing other duties as assigned by the Vice President for Enrollment Management or designee. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: • Master’s degree • 1 to 3 years of supervisory experience as well as progressively responsible experience in higher education, student affairs, or a related field PREFERRED QUALIFICATONS: • Master’s degree in higher education, student affairs, counseling, business, or a related field. • 5-7 years of progressively responsible supervisory experience. • Previous grant writing and management experience. SALARY RANGE: • $67,000 - $72,000 depending on experience and qualifications. SPECIAL COMMENTS: • Sponsorship not available for this position. • This position is 100% grant funded. Continued employment is contingent upon grant funding. TO APPLY: Applications must be made at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu . Please attach a cover letter, resume and the names and contact information of at least three professional references. First review for this position will begin on October 5, 2026. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may be directed to John Allred at john.allred@bhsu.edu . Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu . title: Help Desk Analyst
description: Black Hills State University seeks applicants for a Help Desk Analyst in our Network and Computer Services department. This position serves as a key customer-facing member of the Information Technology team and requires exceptional customer service, communication, and problem-solving skills. RESPONSIBILITIES: - Manage university Help Desk operations and ensure faculty, staff, students, and other customers receive timely, professional, and courteous technical support; - Interview, select, train, schedule, supervise, and evaluate Help Desk student employees; - Develop, maintain, and revise Help Desk protocols, procedures, technical documentation, knowledge-based articles, and service standards; - Administer and support assigned systems, including TeamDynamix and the Druva endpoint backup system; - Coordinate TeamDynamix administration, standards, and processes with other South Dakota Board of Regents administrators; - Configure and deploy computers for faculty and staff and support state-owned computers, applications, printers, scanners, and peripheral devices; - Apply and maintain operating system patches, hotfixes, updates, and upgrades; - Create, test, maintain, and deploy standardized computer images; - Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, account-access, connectivity, and network-related problems; - Manage file permissions and security for network shares; - Plan, test, document, and implement system upgrades and related procedures; - Accurately document, categorize, prioritize, track, and escalate service requests; - Provide end-user support by telephone, email, live chat, remote-support tools, and in person; and - Maintain positive, professional relationships and communicate clearly with university customers and technology staff. KNOWLEDGE OF: - Microsoft Windows operating systems; - Microsoft 365 applications; - macOS operating systems and applications; - Networking concepts, protocols, connectivity, and troubleshooting; - Computer design, installation, configuration, compatibility, and operating system principles; - Information security concepts, practices, and principles; - A diverse range of computer hardware, software, and peripheral devices. ABILITY TO: - Explain technology and information security issues clearly to nontechnical individuals; - Communicate clearly, concisely, and professionally with students, parents, faculty, staff, administrators, and other stakeholders; - Provide courteous and effective customer service to individuals with varying levels of technical knowledge; - Supervise, train, mentor, and support Help Desk student technicians; - Assist with planning and implementing campus-wide technology projects; - Diagnose and resolve technical problems independently; - Collaborate effectively with BHSU technology and support staff; - Develop and implement system-wide technology solutions; - Anticipate potential issues and take appropriate preventive action; - Collect, evaluate, and analyze technical information from multiple sources and system components; - Maintain current technical knowledge of hardware, software, security, and industry developments; - Research, evaluate, and implement innovative technologies; - Lift and move computer equipment weighing up to 50 pounds. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: - A bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience is preferred. CERTIFICATIONS: - The Lenovo Certified Warranty Technician exam will need to be completed in the first three months of employment. REQUIRED LICENSE: - A valid driver’s license is required. COMMENTS: This is a full-time, 12-month, overtime-eligible position. Normal working hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Travel is required. The position is performed primarily in office and classroom environments and includes supervising and directing Help Desk student technicians.  Sponsorship is not available for this position. title: Assistant Professor, Biology (Organismal Zoology)
description: The School of Natural Sciences at Black Hills State University invites applicants for a full-time, tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in organismal zoology, beginning August 2026. The successful candidate will join a diverse Natural Science department and complement other faculty in areas of ecology, evolution, physiology, genetics and cell-molecular biology. DUTIES: The successful candidate will help shape and grow the new wildlife emphasis within the Biology major by teaching upper-level courses that support wildlife students (ecology, mammalogy, herpetology, ichthyology, environmental policy, etc), as well as introductory courses in Biology as needed. We seek a broadly trained wildlife biologist or ecologist who will complement existing faculty strengths in the School of Natural Sciences and develop collaborations with local and regional agencies. Individuals with expertise in wildlife or fisheries management are especially encouraged to apply. Primary responsibilities include successful teaching and advising, development of a research program that includes undergraduate and graduate students, and service related to student professional opportunities. Other opportunities include supervision of graduate students in the Integrative Genomics MSc. program, and course instruction in the Sustainability MSc. program. QUALIFICATIONS: A PhD in Biology, Wildlife Ecology, Natural Resources or related field. ABD accepted. COMMENTS: The School of Natural Sciences at Black Hills State University is a vibrant, growing division with approximately 23 faculty members in biology, chemistry, geology, and physics. Faculty emphasize undergraduate teaching and mentoring, and conduct research involving students in multiple biological and environmental disciplines. Projects are funded through a variety of state wildlife, federal agency, and partnership grants. Research resources include the largest Herbarium in the state, and well-equipped laboratories including a scanning electron microscopy lab. The Center for the Conservation of Biological Resources (CCBR) is a shared research laboratory containing research space and commonly used equipment required for genetics and genomics research. WestCore is a Genetics/Genomics sequencing core facility that provides services including NextGen genome, transcriptome, and Sanger sequencing, genotyping, and quantitative real-time PCR services. WestCore also houses a cell culture area and an RNA isolation room. The Black Hills State University Underground Campus (BHUC) at the Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF) in Lead, SD houses Sanford Lab’s low background counting facility, a class-1,000 cleanroom, and an adjoining workspace available for use in a variety of disciplines. Managed by BHSU, the underground campus partners with groups around the globe to create unique opportunities for collaborative research in physics, chemistry, biology, and geophysics. SPECIAL COMMENTS: The successful applicant must be authorized to work in the United States. Sponsorship is not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications must be made online at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Please submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy, statement of proposed research, transcripts, and names and contact information for at least three professional references. Letters of reference/recommendation are not accepted. (Please note, you may need to combine documents into one file to upload into the system.) This position is open until filled with a first review date of June 19, 2026 at 11:00 PM (mountain time). For application assistance, contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549.
